title: Sentry overnight succession debrief - actionable log
body:
TL;DR: Quiet night overall. Two small customer-impacting blips (latency spike on /v1/generate for ~17m, one degraded cache node causing 5xxs for a subset of streaming clients). Both contained by automated fallback and rate-limited requeue. No rollback required. Handing off to day team with a few follow-ups and a proposed runbook tweak (see ACTIONS).

Shift summary (00:00–08:00 PT):
- 00:23 — Alert: route /v1/generate p50/p95 jumped; metrics showed 2–3x tokenization latency. Pager fired (P2).
  - Initial triage: suspected tokenizer worker pool exhaustion on dedicated-inference-3. Confirmed via /metrics: tokenizer-worker-queue-length peaked at 42 (threshold 20).
  - Mitigation: scale-up tokenizers on pool dedicated-inference-3 (manual scale + temp increase to 6 replicas). Autoscaler didn't trigger because pod churn backoff blocked new creates (see root cause notes).
  - Containment: traffic routed to fallback variant model-hosted-a (compatible variant) by routing policy after 8m; latency normalized.
  - Total impact window: ~17 minutes. Customer error reports: 4 customers reported brief degraded streaming.

- 03:41 — 5xx spike in streaming edge for region eu-west caused by degraded cache node (kv-cache-12).
  - Symptoms: burst of 502/504s for streaming sessions that used prefix cache. Upstream logs show connection resets to kv-cache-12.
  - Action: Evicted node from cache ring (automatic eviction attempted but failed due to stuck leader election). Manually forced leader stepdown, rebalanced ring.
  - Effect: 5xxs stopped within ~6 minutes. No data loss.

Monitoring notes:
- Alert noise: tokenizer queue-length alert fired, but autoscaler suppression prevented scale. Root cause likely related to recent kube controller backoff change (PR #342 merged this week).
- Dashboards: updated draft snapshot attached to linked_artifacts; p95 latency for /v1/generate returned to baseline by 00:55.

Customer comms:
- CS pinged 4 impacted customers with incident summary and ETA for follow-up post-mortem. Ticket refs: CS-7812, CS-7813.

Runbook / playbook observations & suggested edits (draft):
- Tokenizer scaling runbook: add step to override controller backoff when queue-length > 30 and emergency-scaler label present. Include kubectl commands and safety checks.
- Cache eviction sequence: add explicit leader-election remediation steps (systemctl restart leader-elections on kv-cache nodes) and a quick check list to validate ring health (kvctl ring-status).
- Canary routing policy: add explicit observable that routing fallback happened (alert on routing-policy-fallback-rate > 0) so we get faster SRE pager if fallback used beyond 5 minutes.

Open action items (ACTIONS):
- ACTION-1 (owner: Marcus Liu) — Investigate why autoscaler suppressed new tokenizer pods despite queue length exceedance. Possibly related to kube controller backoff PR #342. Due: 2027-09-20.
- ACTION-2 (owner: Priya Desai) — Draft tokenizer-runbook emergency override section and add kubectl snippets + safety run (staging test). Due: 2027-09-21.
- ACTION-3 (owner: Diego Ramirez) — Add leader-election remediation steps to kv-cache runbook and add k6 synthetic that simulates leader failure. Due: 2027-09-23.
- ACTION-4 (owner: Aisha Patel) — Coordinate a 30-minute sync with infra-controller team to discuss backoff config and possible rollback window. Schedule by 2027-09-20.

Follow-ups completed during shift:
- Recreated small synthetic load to verify autoscaler response post-scale (manual). Verified tokenizers accepted traffic and queue drained.
- Confirmed cache ring rebalanced and kv-cache-12 reports healthy leader.

Unresolved questions / notes to document:
- Why did controller backoff not allow new pods despite free capacity on nodes? Node-level resource exhaustion was not observed; possible scheduling throttles due to recent node tainting policy.
- Evaluate whether routing fallback window should be 5m -> 3m for latency-sensitive customers. Need product input.

Incident timeline (compact):
- 00:23: Tokenizer latency alert -> paged SRE
- 00:31: Confirmed tokenizer queue spike -> attempted autoscaler restore (blocked)
- 00:39: Manual scale-up -> traffic start routing to fallback model-hosted-a
- 00:40–00:55: p95 normalized, manual cooldown
- 03:41: Streaming 5xx spike -> detected cache node kv-cache-12 resets
- 03:47: Manual leader stepdown + ring rebalance
- 03:53: 5xxs return to baseline

Post-shift recommendations for day team:
- Prioritize ACTION-1 and ACTION-2; both are high-risk for recurrence if autoscaler behavior is unchanged.
- Run the kv-cache leader-election drill in staging (owner: Diego) before next weekend.
- SRE oncall should consider temporarily lowering fallback trigger threshold for premium customers (discuss with product).

Attachments / artifacts (quick list):
- tmp/dashboard-snapshot-20270918.png (attached in drive)
- logs/stack-trace-tokenizer-00-23-zip (S3 ref included in linked_artifacts ticket)
- replay/kv-cache-leader-events-03-41.json (attached)

Notes to incoming:
- Most stable cluster health right now. No ongoing incident. Defer urgent infra-controller changes until sync with infra-controller team.
- If you see routing-policy-fallback-rate > 0 for >5m, escalate to oncall-2 and open JIRA-INC-4892.

Quick checklist for handover:
- [ ] Confirm Marcus scheduled infra-controller sync
- [ ] Ensure tokenizer runbook draft in PR (Priya)
- [ ] Validate kv-cache runbook edits merged (Diego)
- [ ] Flag any premium customer tickets for follow-up in CS queue

End of notes. Short, pragmatic, leaving the day team with clear owners and deadlines.

-- Aisha (oncall 00:00–08:00 PT)
